correctness.rationale: Induction verifies f^n=(t+n,x_i,y_i product_{j=1}^n(x_i-t-j)) and the stated pullback ideal. Restriction to J=(t,y_i-x_i) gives the Koszul complex on H_n(x_i)=product_{j=0}^n(x_i-j) and P(x,n). The first m generators form an A-regular sequence, whose quotient B is the product of k over the finite grid by CRT, since char k=0. Koszul-cone homology gives H_1=ker(P(x,n):B->B); diagonal multiplication has exactly one zero coordinate per witness. The I_n regular-sequence condition is genuinely needed; the result does not assert it for every P.
risk: No claim beyond the regular-sequence domain or about higher Tor.

originality.rationale: Bell proves return times equal bounded polynomial existential zeros and a special square-time first-Tor nonvanishing example; the new result yields general exact first-Tor multiplicities conditionally on regular sequences, not merely positivity. The method is a standard Koszul/CRT deduction and its originality is confined to this exact dynamical quantitative reading.
